name: Grenache Blanc
say: gruh-NASH BLAHN, in Spain gar-NAH-chah BLAHN-kah

lines.s10: Grenache Blanc is the white form of Grenache: green apple, pear and fennel on a full, round body with a warm finish.
lines.s20: Grenache Blanc is the pale skinned sibling of red Grenache, grown across the south of France and north east Spain. It gives a full, round white of green apple, pear and fennel, usually in a blend and now more often alone.
lines.s45: Grenache Blanc gives the white blends of the Mediterranean their body, from Terra Alta in Catalonia to Châteauneuf-du-Pape in the Rhône. It tastes of green apple, ripe pear and mandarin, with a hint of fennel. It is full and round, with soft acidity and a warm finish. France mostly blends it for weight, while Terra Alta and California's Central Coast often bottle it alone, and cold nights in Paso Robles keep it crisp. Pour it with roast chicken, grilled fish or garlic shrimp. It began as red Grenache: a vine whose berries lost their colour, and growers kept it.
lines.sale: Grenache Blanc is red Grenache that lost its colour and kept its body: green apple, pear and a twist of fennel. With the grilled fish or the garlic shrimp, its weight stands up to olive oil and garlic.

glass.lead: Green apple, ripe pear and mandarin with fennel and a touch of honeysuckle, on a full, round body with a warm finish.

ladder.where: Terra Alta's high plateau; the cooler western hills of Paso Robles
Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Roussillon, Priorat and the Swartland

glass.structure: Dry. Acidity low to medium, alcohol high, body full, with a round, slightly oily texture.

home.home: The southern Rhône, Roussillon, the Languedoc and Catalonia, where heat ripens it to a full, soft white of ripe pear, quince and fennel with a bitter almond finish. Mostly it is blended for weight, in steel or old casks; Terra Alta bottles it alone, fresher from its high plateau, and Roussillon also fortifies it.
home.abroad: California's Central Coast, above all Paso Robles, often bottles it alone, typically crisper, with green apple and mandarin, as cold nights hold its acidity. In the Swartland and Paarl it joins Chenin Blanc in Rhône style white blends.

service.temp: 50 to 55 degrees Fahrenheit, 10 to 13 degrees Celsius; a crisp unoaked bottle a little cooler.
service.glass: A white wine glass; a wider bowl for an oak aged or older wine.
service.decant: Usually unnecessary; open it and pour.
service.age: Most within two to four years, while the fruit is fresh; aged Rivesaltes is a different, fortified wine.

with.dish: Grilled redfish with olive oil and herbs
with.why: body for the oil, fennel to meet the herbs
a round white that stands up to garlic
weight for the bird, apple and mandarin to lift it

with.dish: Paella or saffron rice with shellfish
with.why: body and soft acidity suit saffron and shellfish

labels.means: The grape's Spanish and Catalan names, on bottles from Terra Alta, Priorat and Rioja.
A guarantee mark of the Terra Alta region for whites made wholly from this grape.
The southern Rhône white, where Grenache Blanc gives weight beside Clairette, Roussanne and Bourboulenc.
A fortified sweet wine of Roussillon from white grapes, Grenache Blanc among them, aged until amber and nutty.

guest.q: Is this related to the red Grenache?
guest.a: Yes, it is the same vine in a paler skin. Grenache Blanc is a colour mutation of red Grenache, and it shares its liking for heat and its generous body and alcohol.

guest.q: I usually drink Chardonnay. What is this like?
guest.a: Similar in weight, with no butter. Expect green apple, pear and a little fennel, a round feel and a warm finish, usually with little or no new oak.

guest.q: Is Garnacha Blanca the same grape?
guest.a: The same. Garnacha Blanca is its Spanish name and Garnatxa Blanca its Catalan one, and Terra Alta in Catalonia is where you will most often see it bottled alone.

compare.tell: Roussanne is more perfumed, with honeysuckle and chamomile tea and a fresher finish; Grenache Blanc is plainer, broader and warmer, with green apple and fennel.
Viognier is loudly scented with apricot and honeysuckle; Grenache Blanc is quiet on the nose, with green apple, pear and fennel.
Macabeo, the Viura of Rioja, is lighter and leaner, with less alcohol; Grenache Blanc is fuller, rounder and warmer on the finish.

profile.st: Pale straw to gold · Body full · Acid low to medium · Alcohol high · Dry, or fortified and sweet as Rivesaltes
profile.fruit: Green apple, ripe pear, mandarin, white peach; quince from warm sites
profile.other: Fennel, aniseed and liquorice, honeysuckle, a bitter almond finish; walnut where it is aged in air; a round, slightly oily feel
profile.tell: A full, round, warm white that is quiet on the nose: green apple, pear and fennel, with a faint bitter almond finish
profile.regions: Southern Rhône (Châteauneuf-du-Pape blanc), Roussillon and the Languedoc; Terra Alta, Priorat and Rioja as Garnacha Blanca; California's Central Coast; the Swartland
profile.confuse: Roussanne and Viognier are more perfumed; Macabeo is lighter and leaner; Marsanne is waxier, with almond and honeysuckle; Chardonnay has more acidity and a cellar accent

cards.front: Grenache Blanc: what is its Spanish name, and its Catalan stronghold?
cards.back: Garnacha Blanca, in Catalan Garnatxa Blanca. Terra Alta, inland in the south of Catalonia, bottles it alone under a guarantee mark of its own.

cards.front: In the Swartland, which grape leads the white blends Grenache Blanc joins?
cards.back: Chenin Blanc, with Clairette, Roussanne and Viognier beside it, fermented and aged in old casks or concrete: waxy, nutty and dry, the Cape's answer to a white Châteauneuf.

cards.front: How is Grenache Blanc related to red Grenache, and when did it reach California?
cards.back: It is a colour mutation of red Grenache. It reached California in 1992 as cuttings from Châteauneuf-du-Pape, and was bottled there under its own name about ten years later.

questions.q: A guest orders a white Priorat, rich and stony with ripe pear and fennel, and asks which grape leads the blend. Which do you name?
questions.exp: Garnacha Blanca is the lead white grape of Priorat, for rich, stony, textured whites. Macabeu and Pedro Ximénez are its partners there, and Parellada belongs to the Penedès and Cava.

questions.q: A guest asks which grape gives a white Châteauneuf-du-Pape much of its weight and roundness. Which is it?
questions.exp: Grenache Blanc brings body, roundness and alcohol to the southern Rhône's white blends. Picpoul is permitted there too, but it is grown for sharp acidity, not for weight.

questions.q: After dinner a guest orders a fortified sweet wine from Roussillon, made from white grapes and aged for years in contact with air until nutty. Which is it?
questions.exp: Rivesaltes Ambré is made from white grapes such as Grenache Blanc and aged in air until amber and nutty. Rimage and Grenat are young, fruit led reds, and Beaumes-de-Venise is in the Rhône.

report: Mode contrast, as the plan fixes it: the southern Rhône, Roussillon and Catalonia against California's Central Coast, with the Swartland and Paarl beside it.

A new grape: the profile is written in the manner of GRAPES, and the seven targets are the Rhône, Languedoc-Roussillon, Priorat, Rioja, the Central Coast, the Swartland and Paarl, each a place the entry or the Codex's own region records name for the grape. Terra Alta has no page in REGIONS, so it is named in prose only.

No Codex record is contradicted. The Codex already holds Garnacha Blanca as a grape of Rioja and Catalonia, Grenache Blanc in white Châteauneuf-du-Pape and in the ambré styles of Rivesaltes, and fennel in the whites of Priorat.

The arrival in California in 1992 and the separate label name of 2002 stand on the Rhône Rangers and on the Paso Robles Wine Country Alliance. Terra Alta's share of the world's vines was left out as volatile.

The ladder has two rungs: the grape has no cool home. Terra Alta and an early picked Central Coast wine are placed moderate for the fresher glass they give, which is as much height and picking date as climate.
Say follows the Court's own gruh-NASH for Grenache. The grilled redfish is the one dish from the Creole table.
The sources were read through search results; this session could not open the hosts directly.

The worlds reading of 11 November 2026 moved Grenache Blanc to home and abroad, with plan.json: the New World side is a handful of Central Coast bottles, and the Codex's own Swartland and Paarl records hold it only as a part of white blends, too thin to set beside the Rhône. The blind call of fennel against mandarin also leaned on one style of one valley. The worlds question became a question on the white of Priorat, from the Codex Priorat record.

checked.verdict: Sound after six fixes. The colour mutation, the cuttings of 1992 from Châteauneuf-du-Pape, the guarantee mark of Terra Alta for wines wholly of the grape, Rivesaltes Ambré from white grapes aged in air, and the Swartland were confirmed; Paarl stands on the Codex's region record.
changed: lines.s45: California picks early to keep it crisp now reads cold nights keep it crisp. No source read says the grape is picked early in California; what the sources say is that the climate there gives both rich texture and crisp acids, and the Codex's region record reads inland Paso Robles as hot by day and cold by night.
worlds.contrast.new.cellar: picked early to hold acidity is struck for the same reason; the line now opens on the vessels and says little new oak.
worlds.contrast.why: cool nights and earlier picking now reads cold nights help it hold its acidity.

glass.ladder, the moderate rung: California's Central Coast, picked early, now reads the cooler western hills of Paso Robles. The other three Rhône whites of this chunk put the Central Coast on the warm rung; the cooler west of Paso Robles, on limestone, is where the grape was first planted there.

cards[2].back: gained its own name on American labels in 2002 now reads was bottled there under its own name about ten years later. The year of the label approval was not confirmed (one source gives varietal bottles since 2002; none read gives the date of the approval).
open: The year the grape name was approved for American labels stays unsettled: 2002 in the author's sources, unconfirmed here.
Fennel stands on the Codex's record of Priorat whites and on Spanish notes; liquorice on California notes. The Rhône body's page was not found to name fennel.
Terra Alta sits on the moderate rung for its height, as the author says; its summers are hot.
